The line between the two tabs: Flow shows what is counted from map cards — statuses, marks, edges, and the status loop (#vi-flowtab). Measure shows what is counted from the pipeline log, the conversations and the background jobs: cost, failures, waits, and the gauges of metric kill criteria.

A time window at the top applies to every panel (#vi-measure-scope). A rail on the left lists the panel questions in groups. A red dot in the rail marks a question whose panel has a mark outside its band. The main column opens with one row of kill-criterion gauges (#vi-measure-kill), then the panel groups cost, failures and waits.

**Rules for every panel.**
- **One question.** The question is the panel title.
- **Transform first.** A panel shows a fold over the logs, not raw events: per unit of size, a distribution (median, 90th percentile, maximum), a window, or a ratio.
- **Legend.** Every panel names its marks, its lines and its band.
- **Colour marks the outlier.** A mark outside the reference band has its own colour, so a person finds it without a click or a hover.
- **Drill-down.** A mark opens the items behind it: the tickets, cards, and transcripts. A card opens on the map by the click rule of the flow tables (#vi-flowtab-click).
- **Reference band.** Each panel compares against its own history (#vi-flow-ms-ref).
- **Live.** A panel redraws when the pipeline log or the decision log gets an event.
- **Look.** The panel images on the child cards show layout and marks, with made-up data. The type, colours and spacing follow the visual system of the rest of the tool.

A panel that compares two pipeline variants waits for the replay set (#ms-replay).

card ms-cost  [decided]
Each stage records its cost in dollars and wall time, at the finest grain it can attribute
why: Tokens alone mislead: a cache read costs about a tenth of a fresh input token. Dollars add up across stages and across models. Token counts do not.
subtree: 2 cards, 2 decided

- **Unit.** Dollars, with input, output, cache-read and cache-write tokens as the breakdown. Wall time beside it.
- **Plan, card refinement: per card.** Each conversation has a home card (#werk-mc-split), and each turn names the card that is open on the map. So each turn's cost goes to one card. A turn with no card goes to its day.
- **Plan, spec and tickets: per spec** (#st-spec).
- **Build: per ticket**, the effort that #lp-trend-primary records. The merge loop's cost is per run (#st-build-run).
- **Size.** Each cost is also shown per unit of size: per decided card in plan, per spec story in build (#lp-trend-size).
- **Shape.** A distribution: median, 90th percentile, maximum. Not a mean, because one runaway ticket hides in a mean.
- **Threshold.** None at first. The first 10 tickets and the first 30 days of card refinement set the base.

I checked the main numbers in my last answer again:

- **The $190 saving:** cache writes ($340) plus output ($115), times the Opus share (about 85%), divided by 2. The result is about $193. Cache reads cost the same on both models, so they are not in the saving.
- **The model setting:** all 5 `settings.json` files show `claude-opus-5-5` with no advisor.

One uncertainty: I did not check whether chat subagents use the pane's model. If they do not, the $146 of subagent cost will not change, and the saving will be smaller than $190.

Summing the whole tree when the step ends, and writing the sum to the log, keeps the figure after the transcripts expire." --parent ms-cost --status open --who you --body "Problem: a pipeline session may start worker forks and subagents. **An agent answers the skills' questions, not a person.** Both skills stop to ask: `/to-spec` asks whether the test seams are right, and `/to-tickets` asks about the granularity, the blocking edges, and the splits.
